newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Shakeup seen in Australia union pension funds.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Shakeup seen in Australia union pension funds.

text.p: Australia's industry union pension funds are set for a period of rationalisation following the decision by the Transport Workers Union Superannuation Fund (TWUSF) to broaden its member base, a fund administrator said.
"There is no doubt about it, there is bound to be some rationalisation," TWUSF fund secretary Brett Westbrook told Reuters after the fund launched its new membership drive.

Westbrook said there would be rationalisation in the A$6-8 billion industry pension fund sector following TWUSF's move to compete with other industry funds for potential members. The move is likely to be followed by other industry funds, he said.
Westbrook said there were four other transport industry funds besides the TWUSF. The TWUSF is the largest with about A$350 million of funds under management and 145,000 members.

Westbrok said he expected the fund to continue to grow at about 15 percent per annum as it was an attractive alternative pension fund to the funds offered by mainstream financial institutions with lower administration costs.
The TWUSF was the first fund in Australia to receive full public offer status. This means the fund can accept contributions from self-employed people and members' families.
Westbrook said the TWUSF planned to offer an increased range of financial services to its members.
It currently offers home loans to members, along with its pension services.
